slides.headline: Six things we check before anyone says “low T”
slides.sub: A single testosterone number is the most common reason men get the wrong plan.

items.label: Total & free testosterone
items.text: Total can look normal while free — the usable kind — is low.

items.label: Estradiol & SHBG
items.text: Too much conversion, or too much binding, blunts the testosterone you already have.

items.label: Insulin resistance & visceral fat
items.text: Abdominal fat raises estrogen and pushes testosterone down.

items.label: Sleep apnea & sleep debt
items.text: Most testosterone is produced during deep sleep.

items.label: Thyroid
items.text: Low thyroid mimics low testosterone almost symptom for symptom.

items.label: Medications & vascular health
items.text: Blood pressure, blood sugar and several common prescriptions all affect performance.

slides.headline: A normal testosterone number means the symptoms are not hormonal.
slides.alt_text: Myth: a normal testosterone number means the symptoms are not hormonal.

slides.headline: One number cannot rule out a hormonal cause.
slides.body: Total testosterone is a single value in a system. SHBG decides how much of it is free. Estradiol and thyroid change what the same total feels like. A total mid-range with high SHBG and low free testosterone is a different picture from the same total with both mid-range, and the two are told apart on a panel, not on one line of a result.
slides.alt_text: One number cannot rule out a hormonal cause.
